analysis.title: GS Chong - GS Daily | US Risk Off, HF performance // China Industrial Tech 2027 Outlook // Nintendo 2Q // Sony 2Q // China Consumer Durables wrap
key_insights: US equities had a violent selloff on 11/5/2026: NDX -6.36% (worst day since March 9, 2020), S&P -4.36% (worst since 4/4/25), SOX -12% (worst day since 2020).
Nasdaq VIX had its biggest 1-day move since Covid and is back near Liberation Day levels. VVIX rose nearly 45 points, the second largest 1-day rise ever behind Volmageddon.
High Beta Momentum fell 6.2% and is now 51% off the June highs, the worst drawdown in more than 10 years. Many GS AI-related baskets had their biggest down day since the launch of ChatGPT.
ETFs made up 32% of tape volume, the largest share since June. Price action was likely driven by top-down macro instrument pressure, with massive notionals traded across the ETF complex.
Futures closed below the medium-term CTA threshold (7549). GS expects incremental US CTA supply, with the 2.5 stdev estimate from the morning at -$7.48bn of S&P for sale over the next week.

The selloff is concentrated in semiconductors and AI adjacencies as the market recalibrates datacenter (GW) build forecasts and the execution path after this week's election newsflow. Most affected: E&C stocks (datacenter construction), IPP/Power, Neoclouds and Semiconductors.
SOX multiples have compressed by about 50% from the June/July highs. The next investor debate is whether downside risks to GW/capex outlooks have been overpriced.

Desk flows: asset managers were net sellers on steady semis/AI supply. There was no offsetting bid for Hyperscalers/Defensive Tech, which had cushioned the index the previous day. HF flows were roughly balanced while aggressively toggling short books.

China: the US selloff is expected to weigh on Asia, especially tech hardware. Rotation flows are possible into YTD laggards and low-positioning sectors such as Renewables and Consumers. Focus stays on implementation of policy support tools announced earlier this week.

China Industrial Tech 2027 outlook favors the AI robotics supply chain and Data Center Electricals. GS forecasts China grid investment +6% y/y in 2027 and cuts 2026-2030 sector EPS by 5-10% on average, mainly battery and energy storage names on raw-material inflation and margin pressure.
Nintendo 2Q operating profit of ¥73.9bn missed on weak Switch 2 hardware sell-in despite a software beat. GS cuts FY27E operating profit by 6% to ¥401.8bn, keeps Buy and a ¥9,800 TP.

Sony 2Q operating profit of ¥622.3bn beat on record Spider-Man: Brand New Day box office and PlayStation engagement. Management raised FY3/27 operating profit guidance to ¥1,870bn. GS raises its TP to ¥4,800 and keeps Buy.

China consumer durables 3Q26: covered companies reported a weighted average of -5% revenue and -11% profit growth y/y. GS prefers Midea, Anker and Roborock and expects mild domestic improvement in 4Q26.

Global credit: hyperscaler debt issuance year to date is $296bn, above GS's $250bn full-year 2026 forecast and 36% of aggregate capex. GS expects 35% of 2027 hyperscaler capex (about $440bn) to be debt-financed, plus $300bn of project finance. Near-term risk is tilted toward spread widening.
Rating changes: GMD cut to Neutral, RRL to Sell, UOB downgraded to Sell, Jianghai upgraded to Buy, XGimi upgraded to Neutral. Varmora Granito initiated at Neutral.

Sieyuan TP lowered on US Executive Order 14421 regulatory overhang and easing transformer shortages. 2027-30E EPS cut 9-14%.
Huaming TP lowered for US regulatory uncertainty and potential margin pressure on transformer components. EPS unchanged.
Nintendo 2Q operating profit missed on soft Switch 2 hardware sell-in. FY27E operating profit cut 6%.
Sony TP raised after a 2Q operating profit beat and raised FY3/27 guidance. FY3/27-31 operating profit estimates raised 6-9%.
XGimi upgraded to Neutral on rising overseas contribution.
GMD cut to Neutral in the Australia gold equities review, which is cautious near-term on margin and cash impacts.
RRL cut to Sell in the Australia gold equities review.
United Overseas Bank (UOBH.SI) downgraded to Sell on more headwinds than tailwinds.
Varmora Granito (VARO.BO) initiated at Neutral on its premium tiles focus and East India expansion.
Midea, Anker and Roborock are preferred Buy-rated China durables names.

sector_views.rationale: Prefers the AI robotics supply chain and Data Center Electricals. Sector EPS cut 5-10% on average, mainly battery and energy storage.
Prefers Midea, Anker and Roborock. Overseas is outperforming domestic, and gross margin pressure from cost inflation persists.
Cautious near-term on margin and cash impacts. NEM, RMS and CMM are seen as more defensive.
The desk reports continued supply from asset managers and an ongoing recalibration of datacenter build forecasts.

earnings_insights: Nintendo 2Q (reported 11/5/2026): operating profit ¥73.9bn reported, below expectations. Hardware sell-in was soft and software beat. GS cuts FY27E operating profit 6% to ¥401.8bn and FY28E-FY31E by 2-7%.

Sony 2Q (reported 11/5/2026): operating profit ¥622.3bn reported, a beat. Management raised FY3/27 operating profit guidance to ¥1,870bn. GS assumes ¥160/USD and raises FY3/27-FY3/31 operating profit estimates by 6-9%.
China consumer durables 3Q26 (reported): covered companies had a weighted average of -5% revenue and -11% profit growth y/y. GS expects mild domestic improvement in 4Q26 on easing base effects.
China Industrial Tech: GS cuts 2026-2030 sector EPS estimates by 5-10% on average. Sieyuan 2027-30E EPS cut 9-14%.
